verses.text: Trouble’s coming for you, destroyer. Nobody destroyed you. You betrayed people, and nobody betrayed you. Once you’re done destroying, you’ll be destroyed. Once you’re done betraying, you’ll be betrayed.
LORD, show us grace. We’ve waited for you. Be our strength every morning and rescue us when trouble hits.
At the roar of the thunder, peoples scattered. When you rose up, the nations ran.
Your loot will be picked clean like caterpillars picking a field clean. People will swarm over it like locusts.
The LORD is high above everything, because he lives on high. He’s filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
Your days will be steady, full of rescue, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is your treasure.
Look, their bravest people are crying out in the streets. The messengers of peace are weeping bitterly.
The highways are empty. Nobody travels anymore. He broke the agreement, treated cities with contempt, and showed no regard for anybody.
The land mourns and wastes away. Lebanon is disgraced and withers. Sharon turns into a desert. Bashan and Carmel are stripped bare.
“Now I’ll get up,” says the LORD. “Now I’ll rise. Now I’ll be lifted high.
You’ll conceive chaff and give birth to stubble. Your own breath is a fire that’ll eat you up.
The peoples will burn like lime in a kiln, like thorns cut down and set on fire.
You far away, hear what I did. You close by, acknowledge how mighty I am.”
The sinners in Zion are scared. Shaking has taken hold of the godless. Who among us can live with a fire that eats everything up? Who can live with flames that never die?

The person who lives right and speaks honestly, who wants nothing to do with money squeezed out of people, who waves off a bribe, covers their ears at talk of bloodshed, and closes their eyes to evil,
that’s the person who’ll live high up. A rocky stronghold will keep them safe. They’ll have bread to eat and water they can count on.
Your eyes will see the king in all his beauty. They’ll see a land far away.
You’ll think back on the terror. Where’s the one who did the counting? Where’s the one who did the weighing? Where’s the one who counted the towers?
You won’t have to see those fierce people anymore, the ones who spoke in words you couldn’t make out, in a language you couldn’t understand.
Look at Zion, the city of our appointed festivals. You’ll see Jerusalem, a quiet home, a tent that won’t be moved. Its stakes will never come out, and none of its ropes will snap.
The LORD will be there with us in his majesty. It’ll be a place of broad rivers and streams, where no ship with oars and no grand sailing ship will pass.
The LORD is our judge. The LORD gives us our laws. The LORD is our king. He’ll save us.
Your ropes hang loose. They couldn’t secure the foot of the mast or spread the sail. Then people split up a huge haul of loot. Even people who couldn’t walk took a share.
Nobody living there will say, “I’m sick.” The people living there will be forgiven for the wrong they’ve done.
